answer: Latency-Decay Admission. Each new identity must wait out a visibility delay before its actions count: a fresh beacon starts at zero trust weight and climbs a fixed curve per epoch, asymptoting at one. An attacker can't shortcut this because weight is time, not payment. Each fake identity also emits a cheap ember of upkeep—one signed liveness pulse per epoch—and missing it resets the curve to zero, forcing the attacker to pay continuous operational cost per identity, not a one-time fee.
